Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI printer chat. Between 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-04 Kenneth ran live chats connecting a Bambu P1S, a Moonraker in Docker and his Raspberry Pi Klipper printer, and the AI kept telling people something false or unhelpful at the moment it mattered. A session on 2026-11-04 diagnosed the Moonraker runs from the transcripts the AI saw and reviewed the lessons of the three days before. Its notes are in the side-session notes folder of session local_06a35cc1-bf6c-485d-bf62-19ee49343bbe: `moonraker-skill-diagnosis.md` (each 11-04 failure and the text that caused it), `connection-skill-lessons-review.md` (the lessons and why they were not enough), and `failed-scenarios-one-by-one.md` (every failed run since 10-31 in plain words). Read those three first. Kenneth's test for any of this: does the AI guide a person who is stuck, with guesses labelled as guesses, until they connect or choose to stop; not whether the printer connected, and not whether every sentence is true. His standing rules: the standing prompt holds principles only and situational text comes from the app when it applies; a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; the app reports what it observed; never fix a bug not reproduced; no live-model runs without his approval of a specific batch with a cost; OrcaSlicer-owned files are not touched; temporary notes stay untracked. The 2026-11-03 host skills were proven only on Sonnet 5.5 against Docker with a scripted person who already had the key, which is why the 11-04 runs on GPT-5.4 Mini with a person who had no key failed. Branch: jusprin-newui at e27c962864 or later; the connection skills commit is c56ad86be2 and its message records the measurements.

Task:
Give the printer chat its connection instructions before the person starts connecting, and make one instruction file for both print-host kinds.

The problem. The printer chat's AI gets its connection instructions (the "skill" files under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu`, `connect-moonraker`, `connect-octoprint`) only after the first connection attempt: `PrinterConversation::connection_skill()` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`) returns a skill only once `m_connect_tried` is set and, for a print host, once `m_host_type` is known from the first `printer_connect`'s `hostType`; `AgentHost::session_skill()` and the tool-result path in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` attach it to that call's result. Everything the person says before that runs on the standing prompt (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`) alone: the offer to connect after adding, the question about the address, the first attempt. In two live Moonraker chats on 2026-11-04 the failures sat in exactly those turns: the AI asked "Want to connect it?" after the person had already asked (the prompt's `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING` orders that sentence "exactly"), and told a person who had no API key to "type it there" (the prompt's "say briefly to use that form"). The skill also opens with "The rules above still apply", so standing-prompt sentences written before the skills existed win over the skill's facts; the finishing example "It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it" beat the skill's "verified means Moonraker answered, and nothing more" while Klipper was down.

Kenneth's decision (2026-11-04): send the connection skill with the `printer_add` result for every added printer, chosen by the printer's vendor (Bambu or not), accepting that people who never connect carry the text. Chats opened about an existing printer get it on their first request.

What follows, for you to work out:
- Merge `connect-moonraker` and `connect-octoprint` into one print-host skill, since the app no longer knows which the person has when it sends it. The merged text tells the two apart from what the person sees in their browser and from the first error (a 404 from Moonraker's test means OctoPrint and the other way round; both files already say this). It says what a person with no key does: for Moonraker on a home network the usual answer is Moonraker's `trusted_clients` list in `moonraker.conf`, not a key; the key page is at Moonraker's own address and port (`http://<host>:7125/access/api_key`), and Moonraker's docs give that URL without the port; the SSH script `~/moonraker/scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`; OctoPrint always needs a key and shows it under the user's settings. Label each statement as observed in a real run, from documentation (name it), or a guess, as the skills do now. Keep the dated real-run evidence the existing files carry.
- Move the standing prompt's connecting sentences into the skills or delete them, so the skill is not overruled by older text: `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING`, the Bambu-versus-host first-step sentence in `connecting()`, the `credential_requested` line, the "set up manually" remnants if any, and the finishing example for a verified connection. The rules for a person who declines connecting still need a home in the prompt. Also take the procedure sentence out of `printer_connect`'s description in `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp` ("until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this"), which made the AI ask permission to try an address it had worked out and the person had said to try; keep the description to what the tool does and takes. `tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json` is a copy of the registry and must match.
- Update `connection_skill()`, the attach points in `AgentHost.cpp`, `Agent/AgentProtocol.hpp` (skill triggers), the guard tests in `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp` (the connection-skill cases around lines 3005-3230 and the two "names only states seen from a real host" guards around lines 3370-3490), `AgentUI/src/skills.test.ts`, `App.test.tsx`, `PrinterPanelApp.test.tsx`, and `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s `add_connection_skill`, which mirrors when the app adds the skill. `issue_report_open` is offered only with the Bambu skill and its footer names Bambu Lab; keep that as it is.
- Adding the text at add time may pull the model toward connecting in chats about something else: a wording change did that in 4 of 18 add runs on 2026-11-03 (see the message of commit c56ad86be2). Measure the add cases in `tests/printer_prompt` before and after on the suite's usual cheap model, and report the counts.

Done means: the skill is present from the first connecting turn in every kind of printer chat (add, change, connect), the tests say so, the add cases have not regressed, the three skill files are two, the standing prompt and the connect tool's description carry no connecting procedure, and a live run has been proposed to Kenneth with a cost estimate: a scripted person who does not have the answers (no key and no idea what one is; the Mainsail port instead of Moonraker's; Klipper down; a `.local` name) on the cheapest model the product offers by default, judged by where the person ends up. Run no live model without his approval of that batch. Rules: no OrcaSlicer-owned files; text the model reads says "the app", never Orca; notes untracked and never hidden from `git status`; check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` before building, one build at a time with `-j4`; commit only when Kenneth says so.

Coordination: another session, "Sweep connection messages that omit what the app knows" (local_85842855-5abd-41ec-8462-c9e0cf1fa7b0), is listing places where the app's connection messages leave out facts it holds (Klipper's state after a verified Moonraker test; whether a key was sent before a failure). It fixes nothing until Kenneth confirms, but its fixes would touch `PrinterConversation.cpp`, `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` and the Moonraker skill's "verified" sentence. Before editing those, message it with SendMessage to agree who edits what, and leave the "verified" sentence's wording about Klipper's state to it unless Kenneth says otherwise.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_262aaa6e-aa9c-48de-868d-d4285742aa4c

items.content: Read diagnosis notes and current code
Coordinate file ownership with sweep session
Measure add cases before the change
Merge host skills into one file
Move connecting text out of prompt and tool description
Send skill with printer_add and first request
Update guard tests and prompt-test mirror
Build, run tests, measure add cases after
Write live-run proposal with cost

# Why the Moonraker connection skill did not guide the two live Klipper runs (2026-11-04)

Diagnosis only; nothing edited. Runs: openai/gpt-5.4-mini via OpenRouter, build of jusprin-newui at e27c962864. Transcripts as the model saw them: `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cf7649d3-46dd-4047-a831-32851ae18292/scratchpad/report/{moonraker,raspberrypi}-live-chat.md`. The model's web-search results are not in the transcripts (only a "web search" marker), so what it read there is not verifiable.

## The one fact that frames everything: when the skill arrives

The skill is attached to a request only when that request carries the result of a `printer_connect` or `printer_connection_status` call (`Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3136-3139`), and only once `connection_skill()` knows the host type, which is set by the first connect attempt (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:483-494`). So in both runs the model answered the opening message, added the printer, offered to connect, asked for the address and made the first connect call on the standing prompt alone. The skill's first chance to speak was the reply to "credential_requested". Verified from code and from where "[connect-moonraker skill added here]" sits in both transcripts.

The skill opens with "The rules above still apply." Where the standing prompt gives an exact sentence and the skill gives a fact that contradicts it, the exact sentence won every time (failures 1 and 6 below). The standing prompt is built in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`.

## Failure by failure

### 1. "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" after the person had already said so (both runs)

What the model saw: the standing prompt's connecting rule, `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING`: "after adding, offer it once: end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly 'Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?' and then 'Choices: Connect it | Not now'". No condition on whether the person already asked. Both opening messages said "I want to connect it so I can send prints to it." The conduct rule "When the person plainly states what to do ... do it: call the tool without asking again" conflicts, and the literal "exactly" rule won 2 of 2. The skill was not yet in force.
Verified: the model's text matches the prompt's sentence character for character.
Kind of change: standing prompt, not skill. The offer needs an exception for a person who already asked, or the model needs leave to go straight to asking for the address.

### 2. "If you want, I can try that address now" after "can you just try it?" (run 1)

What the model saw, three texts pointing the same way:
- `printer_connect` description (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1631-1632`): "pass only hostType and the address the person gave, and until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this."
- Connecting rule: "ask for the address they open it with in a browser ... then call printer_connect".
- Conduct rule: "When you are guessing ... ask and wait for the person's answer before adding, changing or connecting one."
The 7125 address was the model's own guess, never "the address the person gave", so by those texts it had to ask first even though the person had said "just try it". The skill's "When they want to try again, call printer_connect again with the address to use" does not say whose address counts.
Inferred: consistent with every text the model had; its reasoning is not visible.
Kind of change: tool description and skill. An address the model derived and the person agreed to try is an address to use.

### 3. "Moonraker is there, but it rejected the key" when no key was typed (run 1)

What the model saw: "Connection to Voron 2.4 350 failed: The print host test failed: HTTP 401: {...}". The app's `connect()` has the credential string the form was submitted with (`PrinterConversation.cpp:826-833`) but the note never says whether it was empty. The skill says 401 is "the same answer for no key and for a wrong key" and "wants an API key, or a different one"; nothing told the model which branch it was in, and its own two previous replies had told the person to "type it there", so it assumed a key was typed. Those replies came from the standing rule "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form", which frames the form as something to fill; the skill's "The field can stay empty" (step 3) was in context for the first of them and did not change the wording. The form label itself says "API key (if the printer asks for one)" (`components/PrinterPanel.tsx:187`), but the model never sees the form.
Verified: the note lacks the fact. Inferred: that this is why the model picked "rejected".
Kind of change: app note after a 401 says whether a key was entered. Skill frames 401 for the common case, a person who has no key and does not know what one is.

### 4. Key URL without the port, then "the key isn't exposed that way" (run 1)

What the model saw: its search returned 

... [2115 characters truncated] ...

e premise survived.
Inferred: that no Mainsail page shows the key is from my search, not from reading Mainsail.
Kind of change: skill. State what is known instead of asking the model to find it: Mainsail and Fluidd do not show the key; the two ways to get it; and that a 401 from a printer on the same home network is most often fixed by adding this computer's network to `trusted_clients`, with no key at all. That is the labelled educated guess a stuck person needs, and the skill has nothing for it.

### 6. "It's connected now, so you can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was shut down or in error (both runs)

What the model saw: the finishing rule, "after the app says the connection is verified ... For example: It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it. You can close this chat now." Both runs reproduce the example almost verbatim. The skill's step 4 says verified "means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board", but the skill defers to the rules above it, and the app's note was just "Connection to X verified." The app has the Klipper state: `Moonraker::test` reads `klippy_state` from `/server/info` and only logs it (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp:90-99`); the backend turns a pass into "verified" with no detail (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:766-776`). In run 2, asked "is it ready to print right now?", the model answered correctly that it could only see that Moonraker answered, so it had understood the skill; the finishing example had already made it say the opposite.
Verified.
Kind of change: app note carries `klippy_state` (already read); finishing example stops promising sending; or the skill's fact is made a rule that outranks the example.

### 7. The "send a report" card after the second failure, although the 401 was progress (run 1)

What happened: `connection_failed()` shows the card on exactly the second failure of the chat, `++m_failed_connections != 2`, by design ("The rule is the app's, not the model's", `PrinterConversation.cpp:846-860`). It does not look at what failed. The first failure (Mainsail page) and the second (401 from Moonraker) were two different steps, the second further along.
Verified. Not a skill matter.
Kind of change: app rule. Count repeats of the same outcome, or hand the judgement to the model now that it has a skill that says which step each outcome means.

### 8. Generic Klipper kept 250 × 250 although the person said 240 × 225 (run 2)

What the model saw: in add mode the standing prompt has no word about bed size. The scope paragraph that mentions bed size ("A setting the settings tools refuse, such as its bed size, is in its printer settings on this computer") is sent only to change and connect sessions; the settings-tool rules likewise. The finding rules say "Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first." The printer list gives each entry's build volume, so the model could see the mismatch, but no tool sets bed size (`printer_add` takes catalogId and nozzle only) and no rule says what to do with a stated size. The model dropped the fact silently.
Verified from `printerInstructions.ts` (`SCOPE`, `SETTINGS` gated on `!adding`).
Kind of change: standing prompt, add mode. Say that a stated bed size is changed manually in the printer's settings after adding, so the person is told rather than ignored.

## What this says about the skill as a whole

- It cannot guide the part of the chat before the first connect call, by construction. Nothing in it reached the opening offer or the address question.
- Where it states a fact that the standing prompt contradicts with an exact sentence (connect offer, finishing line), the prompt wins. The skill's own first line tells the model so.
- Its failure table says which step each outcome means, which is right, but it stops there. For the one place both runs got stuck, a 401 with a person who has no key, it tells the model what it does not know ("You have not seen where ... show the key") and sends it to search. The search returned docs the model misapplied (port) and a premise it filled with a guess (Mainsail settings). What a stuck person needs here is three labelled guesses the skill does not contain: trusted_clients on a home network; the key page at Moonraker's own address and port; the SSH script.
- Two app notes starve it: the 401 note does not say whether a key was entered, and the verified note drops the Klipper state the test already read.

Sources for the two web checks: [Mainsail FAQ: connection unauthorized](https://docs.mainsail.xyz/faq/mainsail_errors/connection-unauthorized/), [Moonraker authorization docs](https://moonraker.readthedocs.io/en/latest/external_api/authorization/), [Moonraker installation docs mirror (api_key page, fetch-apikey.sh)](https://server.creatbot.com/Gitea/CreatBot/CreatBotMoonraker/raw/commit/6b45c0c1d81093e27ed1b2d1d15f9bd47d0ec3b5/docs/installation.md).

# Connection skills: the lessons of 2026-11-01 to 11-03, and why the Moonraker skill still failed on 11-04

Written 2026-11-04 from the session transcripts on disk, Kenneth's own messages first. Nothing edited. Companion to `moonraker-skill-diagnosis.md` in this folder.

## The sessions where the skill was struggled over

| When | Session | What happened there |
|---|---|---|
| 10-31 to 11-01 | Printer connection agent failure (local_9758d37b) | Kenneth's P1S failed to connect; the app hid the cloud-mode printer and the model invented menus. Kenneth: "think about the nature of this problem… fix the root cause, not the symptom"; "tell me very clearly when you have moved the goalpost"; first raised letting the agent search the web. |
| 11-01 | Live Sonnet chat against the real P1S (local_8fa7e7b8 / dd354d04) | Two live chats after the tool fix went well. Kenneth: "we need a general process that can eventually result in a further improved process when more people are using it… Our current approach of doing all the heavy lifting ourselves is not practically feasible." The agent's own lesson: "producing new evidence should be the last resort"; tool results carry what is true now, a skill carries a procedure. |
| 11-01 to 11-04 | AI agent design for printer setup (local_05f541e9 / 73de5d33) | Kenneth rejected invented jargon ("one file per model", "owners fill the files") and demanded checks against OrcaSlicer's real practice; confirmed the five-point proposal: skill per connection type, added at connect time, chosen by the app; tools report observations; grows by reviewed PR plus opt-in reports; a line is written only for a state made to happen for real. |
| 11-02 | Implement the connection skill and test it on the P1S (local_4a3a2148 and its continuations a419cc62, 136dacb0, c85952ea, e4ed3f35) | The first skill was a state-to-step table; on the real P1S it told a person with the right code to re-check it. Kenneth: "The important thing is if the agent was able to guide the user throughout the process effectively and try to make educated guess… We can't just patch up for this use case. We need a mechanism that can work for most cases." Then: "The goal here is not to connect my printer." Then: "It's you wrote the wrong line… I need you to understand why you made that mistake." Then: for each failure, "lack of information? Wrong information? lack of knowledge? Wrong knowledge? What's the appropriate place to supply what's missing?" |
| 11-02 to 11-03 | Try giving the printer chat model only web_search (local_351e9202 / e0a55af0) | Four Sonnet chats on the P1S with search and no skill: the model never searched once, and stated one false fact the skill knew (a printer with LAN Only off is still heard). Recommendation: keep the skill; search alone added nothing. |
| 11-03 | Same implement session, later (1b6e3f18, ca5a0dfa, cce35003, 86306e20) | Kenneth: "add other skills for other connection types too… apply the lessons you learned from building the skill for connecting bambu." The agent listed seven lessons applied and three not applied. Kenneth caught that web search was left out of the host skills; the agent called it "a mistake, not a reasoned choice". Seven Sonnet 5.5 chats against Docker hosts all connected. Kenneth later asked why the prompt still singled out Bambu. |
| 11-02 | Fix Bambu connect tools; Tool results method (local_7d426a6b, b2d2c400) | Kenneth's test for a tool-result bug: a person stuck, told something false, right step hidden, at a cost beyond one more call. Four rules: forward the source's error; else say what the code tested; no new checks; no OrcaSlicer files. |

## The lessons, as they were stated

From Kenneth's words:

1. **Judge by the stuck person.** A skill is good if the agent guides a person who is stuck and makes labelled educated guesses. Not: whether the printer connected, whether every state is covered, whether a sentence is false.
2. **Nature of the problem, not the case.** No patch for one line; ask what stopped the model reasoning.
3. **A process that improves with use.** Verified content is not a precondition for shipping guidance; reports and PRs improve it.
4. **Search instead of guessing**, with the tool present in every chat.
5. **Classify each failure**: lack or wrong *information* (what the app knows at that moment) goes in the app's note or tool result; lack or wrong *knowledge* (how things work) goes in the skill; how to work in general goes in the prompt.
6. **Own the line you wrote** and say why you wrote it.
7. **Nothing situational in the standing prompt; a rule about one tool in its description** (older, restated in every brief).
8. **Tools report what the app saw**, forwarding the source's words.

From the agent's analysis that Kenneth approved by pressing "Yes, build it": the skill explains how the connection works; the prompt holds one way of working (likeliest guess labelled, cheapest check, drop what is ruled out, never repeat a failed step); the app reports what it observed; tests judge how the chat ends.

From the agent's 11-03 list of lessons applied to the host skills: explain, don't tabulate; write a fact only after it happened for real; app reports observations; one signal can have several causes; passing one step says nothing about the next; label guesses and state no menu paths; app picks the skill at connect time. Listed as **not applied**: tests that judge where the chat leaves the person; a real person on a real network as the test case (Docker gave "clean, induced failures").

## Were the lessons applied to the Moonraker skill? Failure by failure

| 11-04 failure | Lesson that covers it | Applied? | What I found |
|---|---|---|---|
| Redundant "Want to connect it?" | 7 (prompt holds principles) and the conduct rule "when the person plainly states what to do, do it" | **No.** The offer is an exact sentence ordered by the prompt with no exception. Kenneth's 11-03 question "do we still have Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once…" pointed straight at this line; the answer defended the Bambu sentence next to it and nobody re-read the offer against lesson 1. Verified from `printerInstructions.ts` and the 11-03 22:14 reply. |
| "If you want, I can try that address now" | Proposal point 3: tools never carry the procedure | **Partly.** The connect tool's description still says "until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this", a procedure rule, and it outranked the person's "just try it". Verified from `ToolRegistry.cpp:1631`. |
| "It rejected the key" with no key typed | 5: lack of information goes in the app's note | **Applied to Bambu only.** The Bambu failure note got the port look; the host failure note never got "the form was submitted empty" or "with a key", although `connect()` holds the credential. The lesson was fixed into one note, not turned into a rule for every connection type's note. Verified. |
| Key URL without the port; "the key isn't exposed that way" | Explain how it works; 4 (search) | **Applied at the wrong level.** The skill explains the app's path to Moonraker (port 7125 vs the Mainsail page) and never the person's path (Moonraker's own pages, the key page included, are at Moonraker's port). Search then returned docs that omit the port, and nothing in the skill let the model apply them. The 11-03 "not applied" item, a real person on a real network, is exactly this: Docker never produced a person who had to find the key. Docs omitting the port: verified. Causal link: inferred. |
| "Mainsail's settings page", never searched | Label guesses; state no menu paths; 4 | **The guard caught the wrong thing.** The evidence test bans menu arrows and "Settings >" so the writer wrote "You have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key, so search for where their version shows it". That sentence presupposes Mainsail shows the key; my search found no such page (Mainsail's 401 FAQ points to `trusted_clients` in moonraker.conf). The guard stops stated menus but not presupposed ones. Same shape as 11-02: the writer kept the "don't be false" half of Kenneth's test and dropped the "a person stuck" half, which is recorded in memory as the 11-02 lesson and repeated here. Inferred. |
| "You can send prints straight to it" while Klipper was down | Skill step 4 says verified means only Moonraker answered; 8 (app reports what it observed) | **Applied in the skill, defeated by the prompt.** The finishing rule's worked example is that exact sentence, and the skill opens with "The rules above still apply". On 11-03 Sonnet 5.5 followed the skill ("verified only means Moonraker answered"); on 11-04 GPT-5.4 Mini followed the prompt's example. The design left a contradiction for the model to resolve, and which way it goes depends on the model. The app also reads `klippy_state` and drops it (`Moonraker.cpp:90-99`). Verified. |
| Report card after the second failure | Proposal point 4: "failed twice" | **Applied as written**, never re-examined against lesson 1. A 401 after a wrong-port failure is progress, and the count cannot tell. Verified from `PrinterConversation.cpp:849`. |
| 250 × 250 bed kept | none of the connection lessons | Add-mode prompt gap, outside the skill work. Verified. |

## Why the lessons were not enough

1. **They were proven on one model with a person who knew the answers.** The seven 11-03 chats ran Sonnet 5.5 against Docker hosts, and the scripted person had the key, took the port advice, and knew it was OctoPrint. Kenneth's test, a stuck person, was never run for a host. The two lessons the agent listed as "not applied" on 11-03 (judge where the chat leaves the person; real person on a real network) are the two the 11-04 runs failed on. Verified from the 11-03 14:00 reply and the 14:30 results table.
2. **The evidence rule shaped the skill around the app's test, not the person's situation.** "Write only what happened for real" made the skills exact about HTTP codes and silent about what a person with no key does. Docker produces every error code and no stuck person. Inferred, consistent with the guard's contents.
3. **The skill defers to a prompt nobody swept.** Three standing sentences written before any skill existed (the connect offer, "say briefly to use that form", the finishing example) give exact wording the skill's facts contradict. Lesson 7 was recited in every brief and applied to new text only, never to old. Verified.
4. **"Lack of information goes in the note" was fixed once, not made a rule.** The Bambu note got what the Bambu incident needed. No one asked, per connection type, "what does the app know at this moment that the model needs?" The host note lacks the credential state and the Klipper state. Verified.
5. **Search was treated as the fix for knowledge gaps.** The web-search-only experiment showed the model does not search unprompted, and 11-04 showed that when it does search it misapplies docs without framing. Search needs the skill to say what to look up at each stuck point and how to read the answer for this setup. Verified for the experiment; inferred for the framing.
6. **Each generalisation was done by the same agent in the same afternoon**, from one printer family to two others, with the lesson list written from memory ("You offered to help me recall lessons. If any lesson from the Bambu chats is missing above, tell me"). Nothing in the repo records how to build a connection skill; the guidance lives in two memory notes, a commit message, and a guard test. Verified: `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` covers skills versus tools in general and says nothing about connection skills.

## Do we have good general guidance? Not yet. What it would need to say

This is a proposal, derived from the lessons above; none of it is agreed.

1. **Start from the person's three stuck moments, not from the app's states**: what address to give; what to do when asked for a credential they do not have; what "connected" does and does not mean. For each, write the likeliest causes in order of cost to check, each labelled as app-observed, documented (with the source), or a guess. The evidence rule applies to facts about the app's own behaviour; facts about the person's side get a source label instead of being left out.
2. **Before writing the skill, audit information against knowledge per connection type**: for each failure the app can report, list what it knows at that moment (was the credential empty, what did Klipper say, which port answered) and put it in the note. The skill is written to the notes that exist.
3. **Sweep the standing prompt and the tool descriptions** for any exact sentence or step about connecting, and delete it or make it conditional, because a skill cannot override "exactly".
4. **Test with Kenneth's test**: a scripted person who does not have the answer (no key, wrong port, Klipper down, `.local` name that fails), on the weakest model the product ships by default, judged by where the person ends up. A run where the person knows everything proves nothing about guidance.
5. **Tell the model what to search for and how to apply it** at each stuck point, since it does not search on its own and misreads docs for this setup.
6. **Decide when the skill arrives.** Today it comes after the first connect call, so anything the person needs before that (the address and port for a Klipper printer) is the prompt's job or the skill's trigger must move earlier.

Sources for the two web checks in the companion note: Mainsail FAQ "connection unauthorized", Moonraker authorization and installation docs.

# Every time the printer chat failed to help someone connect a printer, 31 October to 4 November 2026

Short version, 4 November. Words: the **standing instructions** are what the AI reads in every printer chat. The **extra connection instructions** are added by the app the first time the person tries to connect (the code calls them "skills"); they start with "The rules above still apply", so the standing instructions win a conflict. A **message from the app** is a line the app writes into the chat for the AI, such as "Connection to X failed: HTTP 401". **LAN Only** is the Bambu setting that must be on for JusPrin to connect. The **test program** plays the person from a fixed script and cannot react.

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The app's note then says the connection is verified.

## What the tools report

Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- `started` or `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty means nothing has been heard so far, which is silence and not a finding. The search goes on. After `started`, say you are looking and end your message: the app posts a note when a printer appears, or after about 15 seconds with none, and starts your next turn. Reading the status again before then shows nothing new.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `credential_requested` means the form is up. Say to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again, which opens the form.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

# Connecting a Klipper printer through Moonraker

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **Klipper runs the printer, and Moonraker is the program beside it that other apps talk to over the network.** People usually use it through a web page, Mainsail or Fluidd, in a browser. The app talks only to Moonraker.
2. **The person gives an address.** Moonraker's own port, 7125, answers, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125`. The address of the Mainsail page answered too where that page passed the app's requests on to Moonraker, as a usual Mainsail setup does. A Mainsail page that did not pass them on answered with a web page instead. The address can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up gets no answer at all.
3. **The person types an API key into the app's form, if Moonraker asks for one.** The field can stay empty. A Moonraker set to trust this computer's address let it in without a key. One that did not answered HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the same answer for no key and for a wrong key. You have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key, so search for where their version shows it before you say, and ask what they see.
4. **The app asks Moonraker for its server information.** The app's note then says the connection is verified. That means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board, and while Klipper was not running at all.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen against a real Moonraker:

- **HTTP 401 Unauthorized.** Moonraker answered and wants an API key, or a different one. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as Moonraker answers. This came when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, and when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint.
- **"Could not parse Moonraker server response".** A web server answered with a page. This came from a Mainsail page that did not pass requests on. Moonraker's port, 7125, on the same machine is worth trying.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or Moonraker may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a Moonraker that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address, which their router or Mainsail may show, avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the printer and this computer are on the same network, or restarting Moonraker. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again with the address to use.

# Connecting a printer through OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through its web page in a browser. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.
2. **The person gives the address they open OctoPrint at.** It can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up gets no answer at all.
3. **The person types an API key into the app's form.** The OctoPrint tried here answered without a key as well, but only to refuse: HTTP 403, "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. You have not seen OctoPrint's settings, so search for where their version shows the key before you say, and ask what they see.
4. **The app asks OctoPrint for its version.** The app's note then says the connection is verified. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen against a real OctoPrint, or against the same network failures with a Moonraker:

- **HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission…".** OctoPrint answered and got no key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 403 "Invalid API key".** OctoPrint answered and refused the key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as OctoPrint answers. This came when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint, and when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, so a Klipper printer with Mainsail or Fluidd may be what they have.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or OctoPrint may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a server that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the OctoPrint computer and this one are on the same network, or restarting OctoPrint. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again with the address to use.

Add connection skills to the printer chat for Bambu, Moonraker and OctoPrint

The steps for connecting a printer lived in the two connection tools'
descriptions, which every printer chat reads, including chats that only pick a
profile. They now live in skill files under AgentUI/src/skills/: connect-bambu,
connect-moonraker (Klipper printers) and connect-octoprint. The tools say only
what each state means; each skill explains how that connection works and what
tells the causes of a failure apart, instead of listing one next step per
state. An earlier version did that and sent a person back to re-check a
correct code, because the plug-in's code -1 came with a wrong code, with the
right code and with an address that has no printer.

When a skill is added: the app adds it to the conversation, once, the first
time the person tries to connect (a chat opened to connect, a
printer_connection_status or printer_connect call on a saved printer, or the
printer form finished with a printer found on the network). The app picks it
from the connection type; the model never chooses it. For a print host the
type is known from the saved connection or from the first printer_connect's
hostType, and before that neither host skill is sent, because a skill stays in
the chat once sent. That is why AgentSkillUse gains `stays`. The printer
panel's page did not send skills to the app before, so it does now.

The printer prompt's connecting rule says to call printer_connection_status
for a Bambu printer "once the person wants to connect". Worded as "start with
printer_connection_status", it made the model check the network right after
adding a printer instead of offering to connect: 4 of 18 runs of
add-then-undo and add-named-model on DeepSeek V4 Flash, against none of 18
with either the old sentence or the old status description put back, and
none of 12 with this wording.

The printer prompt holds one way of working: give the likeliest explanation as
a guess, ask for the cheapest check, and do not repeat a failed step unless
something changed. A failed connection note reports what the app saw: the
plug-in's code, how long it took, and a TCP look at port 8883 just before the
attempt and right after it failed. A host that never answers is reported as
"The print host test had no answer from <address> after 30 seconds"; the old
text guessed the printer was off the network. For a connected Moonraker or
OctoPrint printer the prompt now says what is loaded is "not known, as a
Moonraker or OctoPrint connection does not report it". It used to say
"nothing", which is false for those connections: in two live chats on
claude-sonnet-5-5 against a real Moonraker the model told the person the
printer reported nothing loaded, and after the change it said it does not know.

Report card: at the second failed connection in a chat the app shows a card
asking whether to send a report to the JusPrin developers. The rule is the
app's, not the model's, and the model is told about the card and the answer in
notes. The card shows exactly what the report holds: the printer model, the
two connection tools' calls and results, the chat's messages, and the host
kind as its connectionType. The access code goes into a form of its own and
never reaches any of those. Text a person types is scrubbed for an API key's
shape and for any run of six or more letters and digits containing a digit,
which also takes out serials. A code of letters alone is not caught, so the
card says "anything that looks like" and shows the text to read. There is no
server yet: "Send report" saves the file under jusprin/connection_reports in
the data folder, and both the card and the model's note say it has not left
this computer. The other trigger in the proposal, the person correcting the
model, is not built because the app cannot detect it from words. A report
leaves out model turns that only called a tool and had no text.

Web search: with JUSPRIN_TEST_WEB_SEARCH set, the Anthropic codec offers
Anthropic's web_search tool and replays its citations and server tool calls.
JUSPRIN_TEST_WEB_SEARCH_LOG logs what was searched and which model the stream
says answered (the chat's model picker showed "Claude Opus 5.5" during runs
configured for claude-sonnet-5-5; the log showed every reply came from
claude-sonnet-5-5). All three skills tell the model to search before it guesses
where a setting is or what a failure means, and to say what came from the web.
Without the variable the tool is not offered.

Dropped option: after a failed connection the prompt told the model to offer
setting up the connection manually. The model offered it in every failed chat
without being able to say what it meant, and the printer chat has no such
path: its only related link opens the printer's profile settings. The offer is
gone.

Removed prompt case: connect-bambu-not-found, which Kenneth asked to have
removed on 2026-11-02 after it failed 0 of 3 runs in the printer live prompt
suite. In every run the model said it was still listening and would wait, and
gave nothing to check, when the case expected it to point to LAN mode or ask
what the printer's screen shows. The class, its entries in the session payload
and CASES lists, and its README entry are removed; the runner loads 39 cases.
The prompt tests now judge where the chat leaves the person, including
failures the skills were not written from.

Tests and harness:
- A guard test takes the states from the tool registry's output schemas. For
  the Bambu skill it fails if the skill names a state the tools cannot report,
  a state with no named real run behind it, or menu wording; for the host
  skills a state may be named only if a real host produced it, and web_search
  is allowed. Violations of each kind were injected and failed first. Trigger
  tests cover both host kinds. The prompt suite's simulated app adds the host
  skills as the real app does, with an offline test.
- --printer-connect-skill, on a real P1S in LAN mode with the real plug-in and
  no model: a chat that only adds a printer gets no skill, a chat about the
  printer gets it with its first status read, a chat opened to connect has it
  on its first request, and the states run through to the access code request.
  The same run with no plug-in shows `unavailable` and the Install notice.
- Every failure the Moonraker and OctoPrint skills describe was produced
  against real hosts in Docker (Moonraker, Mainsail with and without its proxy,
  OctoPrint 1.9.3) through the app's own print host test. --print-host-check
  runs that test with no model and prints what the chat would be told, plus the
  state before and after.
- --printer-live-p1s takes a scenario: lan stops at the access code form,
  wrong-code types a made-up code twice and answers the report card, cloud-on
  waits for someone to turn LAN Only on, and real-code takes the code from the
  form or from JUSPRIN_P1S_CODE and never prints it. The live P1S chat with
  the right code reports the outcome instead of failing when the printer does
  not connect, because a printer can fail for reasons outside the app.
  --printer-live-host plays a scripted person through a live host chat; with
  PRINTER_LIVE_CAPTURE_DIR set it ends by scrolling the chat from the top and
  saving each screen through WebKit's own snapshot, so a whole chat can be
  reviewed as the person saw it. JUSPRIN_TEST_HEAR_NOTHING and the no-printer
  scenario make a P1S chat in which no printer is heard. The P1S live chat
  prints upstream's info dialog when it appears.
- The report card was tested with state tests through the real AgentHost,
  including real strings for the code and key; a page test and a rendered
  screenshot of the card; and a harness check that the real backend writes the
  file.
- The prompt suite's runner takes the vendor of an add case's printer from
  its catalogue id, which is a string. It read the id as a dict whenever the
  model checked the connection, and crashed. The offline test
  test_the_unrun_result_is_the_apps_own now reads ProviderAgent.cpp, where
  the "Not run" text lives. The suite's offline tests pass, 11 of 11.

Not done: no live chat has been run against the Bambu skill's rewritten
version or the new prompt cases (they need a paid batch), and two real failed
connections against a real printer have not been run. A correct access code
has not been tried through the chat by a model. The squashed history was not
rebuilt or re-tested.

This commit touches no files outside the fork's own folders.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6HNJ9NNWX9AEJRF5D6SGQS8

Let a person stuck connecting a Bambu printer open an issue for the developers

The printer chat gets a tool, issue_report_open, that opens the person's
browser on a new GitHub issue in TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin, filled in
with a title and body the model writes. The app adds its version, the
connection type and the printer model, removes printer serials, the
addresses it knows, anything shaped like an IP address, and code-like
tokens (the connection report's without_secrets), and cuts a body that
would take the link past 8,000 bytes. Nothing is posted: the person
submits the page on GitHub, and the result says the page was opened.

The tool is offered only once the Bambu connection skill is in force.
AgentSkillUse gains `tools`, the tools that come into force with a skill
that stays; PrinterConversation::connection_skill() now returns the
trigger and that list. ProviderAgent offers them from the request the
skill is first sent with, including the continuation after the tool
result that brought it, so every provider sees the same list. That chat
pays one prompt-cache miss; no tool search, defer_loading or toolsets.

Tests: tool lists before and after the trigger, never in a project chat
or a print-host chat, the provider loop's continuation, the link's
encoding, cap and redaction. The shell harness's --printer-connect-skill
takes --open-issue to call the tool in the real app.

# Printer panel prompt tests

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), five printer
tools and the four settings tools, and the chat. The header's filament chat
is the same panel with its own prompt (`filamentInstructions.ts`) and the
settings tools alone; its cases are the `filament-*` ones. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same
requests the app sends. It answers the tools the way the app answers them for
a fixed printer, then checks what the model did. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment.

Prompt changes are evaluated on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, served
only by the hosts that answer the app's notes, and on no other model (decided
2026-09-28; see "Which model"). `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is for that model,
`OPENAI_API_KEY` for the judge.

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case
runs several times, in parallel, and reports a count. By default one invocation
runs at most 100 conversations (`RUN_BUDGET`), shared by the cases it runs: 2
each for the 39 cases, and at most 20 for a case run alone. `--runs N` sets
the count per case instead; use it to look closer at one case. By default
every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar. `--verbose` prints every
conversation, not only the failed ones.

## Judging a prompt change

What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
what it looks for: the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74 of 84 on three runs.
The script renders the prompt from the TypeScript source on every run, so
nothing needs building.

1. After a prompt change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout, same
   model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` (any git revision; the page's source is
   read as it was there and the checkout is left alone) the same day. That
   tells the prompt apart from a bad host day, which usually shows as drops in
   untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs; differences of a few
   runs out of 20 are noise, so look for a clear gap. Paired this way, a real
   effect shows plainly: on 2026-09-28 a two-line edit took
   `add-not-now-done` from 19 to 3 of 20 while its own case improved.
4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
   comparison.

Run every case, not only the one the edit is for. The three sessions share one
prompt, so a line written for one of them reaches the other two; a fix is one
whose own case improves while no other case drops.

Every reply in every case is also held to the rules the prompt sets for all
replies: a `Choices:` line the page draws as intended (on the last line, two
to four choices under 30 characters; read as
`replyChoices.ts` reads it), and none of the internal words the prompt rules
out (profile, preset, catalog, a tool's name). A reply that breaks one fails
its run, whatever the case checks.

A few checks are about what a reply says, which no string test can read.
Those ask a stronger model (`JUDGE_MODEL`, pinned) one narrow yes-or-no
question about the conversation's last reply, and the run prints its reason.

class ClaudeTurn(ApiTurn):
    """One turn on the Claude Code CLI (claude_cli.Run): the turn so far goes
    in once, and the results of each response's calls are its tool results.
    A skill the app adds after them goes in as further text of the last
    result, as the project suite gives the app's notes after a result."""

    def __init__(self, conversation, turn):
        super().__init__(conversation, turn)
        self.run = claude_cli.Run(conversation.instructions, getattr(conversation.case, "tools", TOOLS), list(turn),
                                  *CLAUDE)

    def next(self):
        return self.run.next_response()[0]

    def answer(self, calls, results, skill):
        if skill:
            results = results[:-1] + [[results[-1], claude_cli.developer_block(skill)["text"]]]
        self.run.answer(calls, results)

    def __exit__(self, *_):
        self.run.close()


class Conversation:
    """One run of a case: the chat as the app would hold it."""

    def __init__(self, case, prompt, key, model, endpoint=ENDPOINT, providers=None):
        self.case, self.instructions, self.key, self.model = case, prompt["instructions"], key, model
        self.endpoint = endpoint
        # OpenRouter's hosts only, none else: which host serves a request decides
        # how a message it does not expect, such as the app's developer notes, is
        # rendered for the model.
        self.routing = {"provider": {"order": providers, "allow_fallbacks": False}} if providers else {}
        self.history = [{"role": "assistant", "content": prompt["opening"]}]  # the page's opening line
        self.log = ["assistant: " + prompt["opening"]]
        self.skills_sent = set()
        self.host_type = ""

    def say(self, words):
        """One turn: the person's words, then the model until it stops."""
        self.log.append("person: " + words)
        turn = self.history + [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": words}]}]
        self.history.append({"role": "user", "content": words})
        if getattr(self.case, "session", {}).get("mode") == "connect":
            self.add_connection_skill(turn)
        self.respond(turn)

    def add_connection_skill(self, turn):
        """PrinterConversation::connection_skill: once the person has tried to
        connect, the skill for the connection type follows the message or the
        results of that moment, once, and stays. A print host's type is the
        saved one, or else the one the first printer_connect names."""
        printer = getattr(self.case, "printer", None) or getattr(self.case, "session", {}).get("context", {}).get("printer") or {}
        # An add case names its printer by catalogue id, the vendor first.
        if isinstance(printer, str):
            bambu = printer.startswith("BBL/")
        else:
            bambu = printer.get("provider") == "bambu" or str(printer.get("model", "")).startswith("Bambu")
        kind = "bambu" if bambu else self.host_type
        if kind not in CONNECTION_SKILLS or kind in self.skills_sent:
            return None
        self.skills_sent.add(kind)
        self.log.append(f"app: (the connect-{kind} skill)")
        message = {"role": "developer", "content": CONNECTION_SKILLS[kind]}
        turn.append(message)
        self.history.append(message)
        return message["content"]

    def note(self, text):
        """The app's own line, as the developer, then the turn it starts
        (AgentHost::start_turn): the person has said nothing."""
        self.log.append("app: " + text)
        self.history.append({"role": "developer", "content": text})
        self.respond(list(self.history))

    def respond(self, turn):
        """The model until it stops. Every call of a response is answered, in
        the order the model wrote them, and all the results go back in one
        request (OpenAIResponsesAgent::next_call). Once a call does not
        succeed, the calls after it in that response are answered not_run
        without running."""
        refused = 0
        with (ClaudeTurn if CLAUDE else ApiTurn)(self, turn) as model:
            for _ in range(MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN):
                output = model.next()
                turn += output
                for item in output:
                    if searched := claude_cli.web_search_line(item):
                        # Kept, as the app sends a response's items back.
                        self.history.append(item)
                        self.log.append(searched)
                    elif item.get("type") == "message" and (reply := output_text(item)):
                        self.history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
                        self.log.append("assistant: " + reply)
                calls = [item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
                if not calls:
                    break
                failed = None  # "tool (call_id)" of the first call that did not succeed
                results = []
                for call in calls:
                    arguments = json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
                    self.log.append(f"tool: {call['name']} {json.dumps(arguments)}")
                    if failed:
                        result, recorded = not_run(failed), False
                    elif (problem := invalid_arguments(call["name"], arguments)) and refused < 2:
                        refused += 1
                        result, recorded = {"state": "failed", "error": problem}, False
                    else:
                        (result, _), recorded = self.case.tool(call["name"], arguments), True
                        if call["name"] == "printer_connect" and arguments.get("hostType"):
                            self.host_type = arguments["hostType"]
                        elif (call["name"] == "printer_connection_status" and result.get("provider") == "host"
                              and result.get("address") and not self.host_type):
                            self.host_type = result.get("hostType", "")
                    if not failed and not succeeded(result):
                        failed = f"{call['name']} ({call['call_id']})"
                    self.log.append("  -> " + dump(result))
                    results.append(dump(result))
                    turn.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": dump(result)})
                    if recorded:
                        self.history += self.replayed(call, result)
                skill = None
                if any(call["name"] in ("printer_connect", "printer_connection_status") for call in calls):
                    skill = self.add_connection_skill(turn)
                model.answer(calls, results, skill)

    @staticmethod
    def replayed(call, result):
        return [{"type": "function_call", "call_id": call["call_id"], "name": call["name"], "arguments": call["arguments"]},
                {"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call["call_id"], "output": dump(result)}]

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

On 2026-10-29 I merged and pushed the chat-history record change (history appended in place, skills kept where they fired) after unit tests, the scripted prompt suite, a request-byte prefix check and a live cache measurement. Kenneth asked afterwards whether I had run live prompt testing for regressions. I had not, and I had not proposed it. He asked whether I should have recognised the need; the answer was yes.
