class AddCase:
    """Adding a printer, on the Add session the app sent in a recorded run: its
    full printer list, and the tools' answers for the printers the case names,
    checked as PrinterConversation::identify and ::add check them. A call about
    any other printer is answered as untested and reported."""

    session = ADD["session"]

    def __init__(self):
        self.added = []
        self.lookups = []  # printer_identify calls that drew cards, by turn
        self.identify_calls = []  # every printer_identify call, drawn or refused
        self.turn = 0
        self.untested = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        nozzle = arguments.get("nozzle")
        said = isinstance(nozzle, (int, float)) and nozzle > 0
        if name == "printer_identify":
            self.identify_calls.append(arguments)
            ids = list(dict.fromkeys(arguments.get("catalogIds", [])))
            unknown = [catalog_id for catalog_id in ids if catalog_id not in CATALOG]
            if unknown:
                return {"error": {"code": "unknown_printer", "message": f'"{unknown[0]}" is not on the printer list; copy it '
                                                                      "exactly from the printer list."}}, False
            if len(ids) > 3:
                return {"error": {"code": "too_many",
                                  "message": "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead."}}, False
            if not all(catalog_id in IDENTIFIED for catalog_id in ids):
                self.untested += ids
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + ", ".join(ids) + "."}}, False
            for catalog_id in ids:
                if said and nozzle not in IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"]:
                    return unknown_nozzle(IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.lookups.append(self.turn)
            return {"printers": [IDENTIFIED[catalog_id] for catalog_id in ids]}, False
        if name == "printer_add":
            catalog_id = arguments.get("catalogId", "")
            if catalog_id in self.added:
                return {"error": {"code": "already_added", "message": "This conversation already added it."}}, False
            if catalog_id not in ADD["printer_add"]:
                self.untested.append(catalog_id)
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + catalog_id + "."}}, False
            answer = ADD["printer_add"][catalog_id]
            if said and nozzle not in answer["printer"]["nozzles"]:
                return unknown_nozzle(answer["printer"]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.added.append(catalog_id)
            return {"printer": {**answer["printer"], "nozzle": nozzle if said else answer["printer"]["nozzle"]}}, False
        if name == "printer_change" and not self.added:
            # PrinterConversation::preflight_tool, before anything is added.
            return {"error": {"code": "no_printer",
                              "message": "No printer is set up in this conversation yet: add one first."}}, False
        self.untested.append(name)
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

    def say(self, conversation, words):
        """The turn's last reply."""
        self.turn += 1
        start = len(conversation.log)
        conversation.say(words)
        replies = [line for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
        return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""

    def outcome(self, printer, reply):
        # Space at a line's end is not shown, the page trims each choice, and a
        # blank line before the choices draws the same chips.
        offered = "\n".join(line.rstrip() for line in reply.rstrip().splitlines() if line.strip()).endswith(CONNECT_OFFER)
        passed = self.added == [printer] and offered
        detail = ("added" if self.added == [printer] else f"added {self.added or 'nothing'}") + \
                 ("; offered to connect" if offered else "; NO CONNECT OFFER: " + repr(reply[-120:]))
        if self.untested:
            detail += "; untested " + ", ".join(self.untested)
        return passed, detail


class AddNamedModel(AddCase):
    """The person names one model plainly. Passes when that printer is added
    and the reply ends with the connect offer and its two choices."""

    name = "add-named-model"

    def run(self, conversation):
        reply = self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        return self.outcome("BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini", reply)


class AddChooseFromThree(AddCase):
    """A name that fits three models, then the person's choice, as a tap on its
    chip sends it. Passes when nothing is added before the choice, the chosen
    printer is, and the reply ends with the connect offer. Looking the chosen
    printer up again draws a second picture card; it is reported, not failed."""

    name = "add-choose-from-three"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "prusa mk4")
        asked_first = not self.added
        reply = self.say(conversation, "Prusa MK4S")
        passed, detail = self.outcome("Prusa/Prusa MK4S", reply)
        if not asked_first:
            passed, detail = False, "ADDED BEFORE ASKING; " + detail
        if 2 in self.lookups:
            detail += "; looked it up again"
        return passed, detail


class AddThenUndo(AddCase):
    """The person names one model, it is added, and they tap Undo on its
    receipt: the app removes it and says so in a note, then the model answers
    with nothing said. Passes when that reply adds nothing, drops the connect
    offer, and asks which printer they have."""

    name = "add-then-undo"
    printer = "BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        if self.added != [self.printer]:
            return False, f"setup: added {self.added or 'nothing'}"
        name = ADD["printer_add"][self.printer]["printer"]["name"]
        # The app's note, word for word (PrinterConversation::undo_add).
        self.added = []  # the printer is gone; another add of it is a new one
        self.turn += 1
        start = len(conversation.log)
        conversation.note(f"The person tapped Undo on the receipt: {name} is removed and is no longer one of their printers.")
        replies = [line[len("assistant: "):] for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
        reply = replies[-1] if replies else ""
        problems = []
        if self.added:
            problems.append(f"ADDED {self.added} AGAIN")
        if not reply:
            problems.append("NO REPLY")
        if "Connect it" in reply:
            problems.append("STILL OFFERS TO CONNECT")
        if "?" not in reply:
            problems.append("ASKED NOTHING")
        detail = "; ".join(problems) or "asked again: " + repr(reply[-120:])
        if self.untested:
            detail += "; untested " + ", ".join(self.untested)
        return not problems, detail


def last_reply(conversation, words=None, note=None):
    """The last thing the model wrote in one turn: the person's words, or the
    app's note."""
    start = len(conversation.log)
    if note is None:
        conversation.say(words)
    else:
        conversation.note(note)
    replies = [line for line in conversation.log[start:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")]
    return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""


def offers_done(reply):
    """Whether the page draws Done as the reply's one chip, reading the reply
    as splitChoices (replyChoices.ts) does: "Choices:" starting a word on the
    last line, with something said before it."""
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()
    found = re.search(r"(^|\s)Choices:(.*)$", lines[-1]) if lines else None
    if found is None:
        return False
    said = "\n".join(lines[:-1]) + lines[-1][:found.start()]
    return [choice.strip() for choice in found.group(2).split("|") if choice.strip()] == ["Done"] and said.strip() != ""


def says_can_close(reply):
    return re.search(r"\b(?:can|may|safe to|okay to|ok to|feel free to)\s+close\s+(?:this\s+|the\s+|your\s+)?"
                     r"(?:chat|conversation)\b", reply, re.IGNORECASE) is not None


class Finishing:
    """When nothing is left to decide, tell the person they can close the chat."""

    def end(self, reply, detail):
        close = says_can_close(reply)
        choices = "Choices:" in reply
        detail += "; says to close" if close else "; NO CLOSE INSTRUCTION: " + repr(reply[-120:])
        if choices:
            detail += "; CHOICES OFFERED"
        return close and not choices, detail


class AddNotNowClose(Finishing, AddCase):
    """The person adds a printer and turns down connecting it. Passes when the
    reply to "Not now" says they can close the chat."""

    name = "add-not-now-close"

    def run(self, conversation):
        self.say(conversation, "bambu lab a1 mini")
        reply = self.say(conversation, "Not now")
        detail = "added" if self.added == ["BBL/Bambu Lab A1 mini"] else f"added {self.added or 'nothing'}"
        return self.end(reply, detail)


class ConnectOutcome(Finishing, ConnectBambu):
    """Connect the saved A1 mini, as connect-bambu does, then the person taps
    Connect on the card and the app reports the outcome in a note."""

    def connect(self, conversation, outcome):

        if not self.card:

---
name: connect-print-host
trigger: connect_print_host
---

# Connecting a printer through Moonraker or OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a printer that is not a Bambu Lab one is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention. Each statement says where it comes from: seen in a real run, a named document, or a guess.

## Moonraker or OctoPrint

The app connects to one of two programs that run beside the printer, and printer_connect needs to know which:

- **A Klipper printer is reached through Moonraker**, the program beside Klipper that other apps talk to over the network. People usually use it through a web page in a browser, Mainsail or Fluidd. The app talks only to Moonraker.
- **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through OctoPrint's own web page. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.

When the person does not know which they have, ask what the page they open to control the printer is called, or what it shows. A guess is fine, because the first attempt tells the two apart: a test for the wrong one got HTTP 404 both ways (seen 2026-11-02, against both in Docker).

## The address

Ask for the address they open that page at, including any port.

- **Moonraker:** the app needs Moonraker's own address, port 7125 unless it was changed, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125`. The address of the Mainsail page answered too where that page passed the app's requests on to Moonraker, as a usual Mainsail setup does. A Mainsail page that did not pass them on answered with a web page instead (both seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). So when the Mainsail address does not work, the same machine at port 7125 is the likeliest next address.
- **OctoPrint:** the address they open OctoPrint at.
- The address can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up got no answer at all (seen 2026-11-02 with a `.local` name no device answered to).
- An address you worked out yourself, such as port 7125 on the machine they named, is a guess: say so. When they say to try it, call printer_connect with it at once, without asking again.

## The key

printer_connect opens the app's form, where the person types a key if they have one. The field can stay empty, and an empty first try is fine: the answer says whether a key is needed. Never ask for the key in chat. After the form is sent, the app tests the connection for up to 30 seconds, and its note says how it went. Answer anything they say meanwhile.

**Moonraker.** A Moonraker set to trust this computer's address let the app in without a key. One that did not answered HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the same answer for no key and for a wrong key (seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). Most people at home have no key and do not know what one is, so after a 401 do not ask them to type one. What helps them:

- **The likeliest fix on a home network needs no key.** Moonraker lets in only the addresses in `trusted_clients`, under `[authorization]` in `moonraker.conf`, its settings file on the printer's computer. Mainsail's own FAQ for its "connection unauthorized" error says to add the network there, written like `192.168.1.0/24` for the addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.254, and then restart Moonraker. That this is their cause is a guess. Where they can edit that file depends on their setup, so search for their version before you say.
- **A key, if they want one.** Moonraker's installation documentation gives the key page as `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key`, with no port. The page is Moonraker's own, so it is at Moonraker's address and port, the one that answered 401, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125/access/api_key`. A page not reached at another port says nothing about the key. The same documentation says to open the page from a trusted client, so a computer Moonraker does not trust may be refused there too. Over SSH on the printer's computer, it gives the script `~/moonraker/scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`.
- Mainsail's FAQ for this error points to `trusted_clients`, not to a key, and no Mainsail or Fluidd page that shows the key was found in their documentation (searched 2026-11-04). Do not send the person looking for one.

**OctoPrint.** It needs a key. Without one, the OctoPrint tried (1.9.3, in Docker, 2026-11-02) answered only to refuse, HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. OctoPrint's API documentation says a user's own key is shown in their user settings, and in the user list of its Access Control settings, and the global key in its API settings. Versions differ, so search for where theirs shows it before you say, and ask what they see.

## When it is verified

The app's note says the connection is verified.

- **Moonraker:** the app asked Moonraker for its server information. That means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board, and while Klipper was not running at all. So do not say the printer is ready to print; say Moonraker answered.
- **OctoPrint:** the app asked OctoPrint for its version. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `credential_requested` means the form is up.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen on 2026-11-02 through the app's own test, against Moonraker, Mainsail and OctoPrint in Docker:

- **HTTP 401 Unauthorized.** Moonraker answered and did not let the app in. The address is right; see the key above.
- **HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission…" or "Invalid API key".** OctoPrint answered and got no key, or refused the one it got. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as the chosen program answers. This came when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, and when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint, so the other one at the same address is the next try.
- **"Could not parse Moonraker server response".** A web server answered with a page. This came from a Mainsail page that did not pass requests on. Moonraker's port, 7125, on the same machine is worth trying.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or the program may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a server that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address, which their router or Mainsail may show, avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the printer's computer and this one are on the same network, or restarting the program. When they want to try again, call printer_connect again with the address to use.

# Writing a connection skill

Draft of 2026-11-04 for Kenneth's review. Nothing here is agreed yet. Where a sentence describes code or a test, it describes what is on `jusprin-newui` at e27c962864; where it proposes a rule, it says so.

A connection skill is the text the app adds to a printer chat when a person tries to connect a printer of one connection type: `AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md`, `connect-moonraker` and `connect-octoprint`. Read this before writing a new one or changing one. The general rules for skills, and for when a skill becomes a tool, are in [Tool extension guide, Skills versus tools](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md#skills-versus-tools); this document adds only what connecting a printer needs.

## What the skill is for

Kenneth's test, 2026-11-02: the skill is good if the agent guides a person who is stuck and makes educated guesses it labels as guesses, until the printer is connected or the person chooses to leave it. It is not judged by whether a printer connected, by how many states it names, or by whether every sentence in it is true. A skill that is never wrong and never helps a stuck person fails the test.

Three times in three days a skill was written to the wrong half of that test. The first Bambu skill was a table from state to next step, and on the real P1S it told a person with the right access code to re-check it. The second Bambu skill said "add no cause of your own", and the model repeated a false reason instead of guessing. The host skills said "you have not seen where Mainsail or Fluidd show the key", and on 2026-11-04 the model told a person who had no key to look in "Mainsail's settings page", which does not show it. Each time the writer kept "say nothing false" and dropped "help the stuck person".

## How the skill reaches the model

Facts about the code today.

- The app chooses the skill from the connection type and adds it to the conversation once, with the result of the first `printer_connection_status` or `printer_connect` call, or on the first request of a chat opened to connect (`PrinterConversation::connection_skill`, `AgentHost::session_skill`). The model never picks it. For a print host the type is known only from the first `printer_connect`'s `hostType` or a saved connection, so a host skill never arrives before the model has asked for an address and called connect.
- The skill stays in the chat once sent (`AgentSkillUse::stays`).
- Everything before that call runs on the standing prompt alone (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`): the offer to connect after adding, the request for an address, the first connect call. A skill cannot guide those turns.
- The skill opens with "The rules above still apply", so wherever the standing prompt gives an exact sentence or an exact step, the prompt wins over a fact in the skill. On 2026-11-04 the prompt's finishing example "It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it" beat the skill's "verified means Moonraker answered, and nothing more", with Klipper shut down.

def run_once(case_class, prompt, key, model, endpoint=ENDPOINT, providers=None):
    case = case_class()
    conversation = Conversation(case, prompt, key, model, endpoint, providers)
    try:
        passed, detail = case.run(conversation)
    except Exception as error:  # a failed request is a failed run, reported as such
        return False, f"ERROR {error}", conversation.log
    # The opening is the page's own line, not the model's.
    problems = sorted({problem for line in conversation.log[1:] if line.startswith("assistant: ")
                       for problem in reply_problems(line[len("assistant: "):])})
    if problems:
        passed, detail = False, detail + "; " + "; ".join(problems)
    return passed, detail, conversation.log


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # the logs show replies as the model wrote them
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])

# Connection skill sent at add time, one print-host skill (2026-11-04)

Uncommitted in the main checkout on jusprin-newui (e27c962864). Nothing committed.

## What changed

- `PrinterConversation::connection_skill()` returns a skill whenever the chat has a saved printer: the one an Add chat just added (so it rides on `printer_add`'s result, or the form's finish turn), or the one a Change/Connect chat is about (so it is on the first request). Vendor BBL gets `connect_bambu` with `issue_report_open`; any other vendor gets `connect_print_host`. The flag that tracked "tried to connect" (`m_connect_tried`) is gone. The project's stock printer gets none. `m_host_type` stays only for the report's `connectionType`.
- `connect-moonraker` + `connect-octoprint` are now one file, `AgentUI/src/skills/connect-print-host/SKILL.md`. It tells the two apart (what the person's page is called; a 404 means the other kind), and says what a person with no key does: `trusted_clients` under `[authorization]` in `moonraker.conf` (Mainsail's FAQ, labelled a guess for their setup), the key page at Moonraker's own port (installation docs omit the port, and say to open it from a trusted client), `~/moonraker/scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`, and that no Mainsail/Fluidd page showing the key was found. OctoPrint: needs a key; where the API docs say keys are shown; search for their version. The Moonraker "verified" sentence is kept word for word, with one added sentence after it: "So do not say the printer is ready to print; say Moonraker answered." (The sweep session owns the Klipper-state wording.)
- Both skills now open by saying when they arrive and that connecting starts only when the person wants it. They carry the after-adding offer, made conditional: "unless they have already said whether they want it connected".
- Standing prompt (`printerInstructions.ts`): removed `OFFER_AFTER_ADDING`, the Bambu-versus-host first step, "say briefly to use that form", the 30-second sentence and the timeout sentence (moved into the skills), and the "It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it" example (now the decline example). It keeps: the tools act on this printer, connecting is optional, never ask for a credential in chat, and the rules for someone who stops.
- `printer_connect` description: no "until they give one, ask for it instead of calling this"; address described as "The print host's address, an IP address or a name, with its port when it has one." `tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json` regenerated.
- Tests: trigger cases rewritten (add, change, connect, form add, stock printer, print host), print-host evidence guard on the one file (adds `credential_requested` from the 11-04 live chats; `trusted_clients` and `[authorization]` allowed as names), page tests (`skills.test.ts`, `App.test.tsx`, `PrinterPanelApp.test.tsx`, `printerInstructions.test.ts`), runner mirror (`add_connection_skill`) and its offline tests, shell harness `--printer-connect-skill` expectations (not run: needs the full app build).

## Measurement batch proposed (not run, needs Kenneth's approval)

1. Add cases, before vs after, same hour: 10 add cases x 20 runs x 2 arms = 400 runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash (pinned hosts), the "before" arm from a worktree at e27c962864. OpenRouter list price $0.091/M input, $0.018/M cached, $0.18/M output; about 50k tokens a run, mostly cached: about $1. Three of the cases call the gpt-5.5 judge: about 120 calls, about $3.
2. Full suite after-run against the 2026-11-03 baseline: 39 cases x 3 runs = 117 runs. Every change and connect case now carries a skill from its first request, so they all read new text. About $1 DeepSeek + about $3 judge.
Total estimate about $8, under $15.

## Live run proposed (not run, needs Kenneth's approval)

Model: GPT-5.4 Mini, the product's default for OpenAI and OpenRouter (`ProviderProfile.hpp`). OpenRouter list price $0.75/M input, $0.075/M cached, $4.50/M output: about $0.10 a 10-turn chat.
Harness: `--printer-live-host <script>` in the real app (one full app build), against Moonraker in Docker set to trust no client, Klipper not running, Mainsail on 8081 without its proxy.
Four scripted people, two runs each (8 chats, about $1):
- no key, does not know what one is ("I don't have an API key. What is that?"), empty form each time;
- gives the Mainsail address and port, never Moonraker's;
- Klipper down: after verified, asks "is it ready to print?";
- gives a `.local` name that does not resolve, then the IP only if asked.
Judged by reading each chat: where does the person end up (connected, or with a concrete next step such as `trusted_clients` or the key page at port 7125), and were guesses labelled.
Gap: the harness opens only Connect chats. An add-then-connect chat needs a small `add <catalogue id>` verb in `queue_printer_live_host`.

## The key

printer_connect opens the app's form, where the person types a key if they have one. The field can stay empty, and an empty first try is fine: the answer says whether a key is needed. Never ask for the key in chat. After the form is sent, the app tests the connection for up to 30 seconds, and its note says how it went. Answer anything they say meanwhile.

**Moonraker.** A Moonraker set to trust this computer's address let the app in without a key. One that did not answered HTTP 401 Unauthorized, the same answer for no key and for a wrong key (seen 2026-11-02 in Docker). Most people at home have no key and do not know what one is, so after a 401 do not ask them to type one. What helps them:

- **The likeliest fix on a home network needs no key.** Moonraker lets in only the addresses in `trusted_clients`, under `[authorization]` in `moonraker.conf`, its settings file on the printer's computer. Mainsail's own FAQ for its "connection unauthorized" error says to add the network there, written like `192.168.1.0/24` for the addresses 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.254, and then restart Moonraker. That this is their cause is a guess. Where they can edit that file depends on their setup, so search for their version before you say.
- **A key, if they want one.** Moonraker's installation documentation gives the key page as `http://{moonraker-host}/access/api_key`, with no port. The page is Moonraker's own, so it is at Moonraker's address and port, the one that answered 401, as in `http://192.168.1.50:7125/access/api_key`. A page not reached at another port says nothing about the key. The same documentation says to open the page from a trusted client, so a computer Moonraker does not trust may be refused there too. Over SSH on the printer's computer, it gives the script `~/moonraker/scripts/fetch-apikey.sh`.
- Mainsail's FAQ for this error points to `trusted_clients`, not to a key, and no Mainsail or Fluidd page that shows the key was found in their documentation (searched 2026-11-04). Do not send the person looking for one.

**OctoPrint.** It needs a key. Without one, the OctoPrint tried (1.9.3, in Docker, 2026-11-02) answered only to refuse, HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. OctoPrint's API documentation says a user's own key is shown in their user settings, and in the user list of its Access Control settings, and the global key in its API settings. Versions differ, so search for where theirs shows it before you say, and ask what they see.

## When it is verified

The app's note says the connection is verified.

- **Moonraker:** the app asked Moonraker for its server information. That means Moonraker answered, and nothing more: it answered the same way while Klipper could not reach the printer's board, and while Klipper was not running at all. What says whether the printer can print is Klipper's state, which the note gives after "Moonraker reports Klipper's state as". Unless that state is `ready`, do not say the printer is ready to print: say Moonraker answered, give the state, and say what it generally means. Only `error` has been seen here, from a Moonraker in Docker whose Klipper could not reach its board ("mcu 'mcu': Unable to connect", 2026-11-04). The rest is general knowledge about Klipper, so say it as such: `ready` is Klipper running and in contact with the board; `startup` is Klipper still starting, so test again in a minute; `shutdown` is Klipper stopped after an error or an emergency stop, and a firmware restart in Mainsail or Fluidd starts it again; `error` is Klipper unable to start, often a mistake in its configuration or a board it cannot reach, and Mainsail or Fluidd shows Klipper's own message; `disconnected` is Moonraker not in contact with Klipper at all.
- **OctoPrint:** the app asked OctoPrint for its version. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

a Responses API endpoint, to compare models rather than to judge a prompt
change, such as:

```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py \
    --model xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro --provider Xiaomi --provider GMICloud
```

A model other than the default starts with no hosts pinned. The judge stays on
OpenAI whichever model answers, so counts are judged alike.

Pin OpenRouter's hosts with `--provider` (repeatable). OpenRouter serves an
open-weight model from many hosts, and they render a message the model was not
trained on differently. The app's notes are `developer` messages, OpenAI's
convention: DeepSeek V4 has no such role in ordinary chat, and hosts that treat
it as a `system` message open no reply turn after it, so the model answers an
app note with nothing or with noise (2026-09-28: StreamLake, Parasail and Relace
empty 3 of 3, DeepInfra junk; Alibaba, Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud correct).
Unpinned, those cases measure which host a request landed on. Check a new
model's hosts with a note as the last message before trusting its counts.

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every request with the locally installed
Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude subscription,
through the project suite's `claude_cli.py`; `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key. See
`tests/project_prompt/README.md`, "Running on the Claude subscription", for
the login, the isolation from the developer's own Claude Code setup and what
differs from the app's request.

```bash
tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case connect-bambu --runs 1
```

The model is `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium` for both, pinned
(`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`). Each turn, started by the person's
message or by an app note, is one CLI run: the chat so far is a session the
CLI resumes, and every call in the turn reaches
the case through the CLI's tool stub. A connection skill the app adds after a
call's results goes in as further text of the last result, as the CLI

  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge
  (`baseline.json`), except the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's
  own (`baseline-claude-cli.json`, which `--backend claude-cli` compares with).
  A claude-cli count is compared only with that one. Changing the judge
  changes what every judged case counts, so the runner will not compare a
  run on another judge with either: such results start their own baseline,
  under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 29 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **Web search**: the CLI's own `WebSearch` is offered before the stub's
  tools, as the app offers its provider's own search after its tools on every
  reply request (since 2026-11-03). The CLI runs a search itself inside the
  response, so the runner sees only its query and the pages it found; a
  response whose only calls are searches is read on to the reply that follows.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Reasoning from what I changed, 35 of the 39 cases can be affected. Only the 4 filament cases can't be.

**Every printer-chat case (35) reads two things I changed.** The standing prompt goes into every printer chat, and I removed sentences from it: the after-adding offer, the "Bambu first, print host first" step, the line about what `credential_requested` means, "use that form", the 30-second sentence, and the "It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it" example. The `printer_connect` tool description goes into every printer chat too, and I changed it. So any of these 35 could reply differently even when connecting never comes up. The 4 filament cases (`filament-*`) use a different prompt and only the settings tools, so they don't see either change.

**Within those 35, some are hit more directly:**

- **The 10 add cases (`add-*`).** The connect offer used to come from the standing prompt. Now it comes only from the skill that rides on the `printer_add` result, and the case fails if the reply doesn't end with that offer. A case where the add fails or is undone (`add-then-undo`, `add-unsupported-printer`, `add-not-now-close`) now has a skill in front of it, or loses one, at a different moment than before.
- **The 13 change cases except `change-stock-copy`.** These chats are about a saved printer that isn't the project's stock one, so the skill is now in the request from the first message, even when the person only asks about the bed size or the nozzle. Before, a change chat never had the skill unless it started connecting. `change-then-connect` is the one where the person actually asks to connect, so its first reply is the most exposed.
- **`change-stock-copy`.** It uses the project's stock printer, so it gets no skill, before or after. It sees only the standing-prompt and tool-description changes.
- **The 12 connect cases (`connect-*`).** They used to get the skill after the first `printer_connect` call. Now they get it from the first message. The skill text changed as well: the Bambu skill got a new opening, a new step 3 and a new first line in its failure section, and the Moonraker and OctoPrint skills were merged into one. The print-host cases (`connect-host-address`, `connect-host-no-response`) read the merged text. Two error messages a tool returns also changed (the invalid-arguments one and the missing-address one), so any connect case that makes a bad `printer_connect` call sees new wording.

So the full-suite run was the right check: no case outside the filament ones can be ruled out.

Thirty cases scored the same. These changed (old → new):

| Case | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `connect-unforeseen-failure` | 8 | 3 |
| `connect-code-ruled-out` | 7 | 4 |
| `connect-port-went-quiet` | 10 | 7 |
| `change-then-connect` | 10 | 7 |
| `connect-screen-says-disconnected` | 7 | 5 |
| `connect-right-code-silent-port` | 5 | 4 |
| `connect-host-no-response` | 10 | 9 |
| `add-unshipped-nozzle` | 10 | 9 |
| `add-many-fit` | 5 | 8 |

**The main loss is in Bambu connect chats.** The judge says a person was "left stuck" in 5 old runs and 18 new ones. In 17 of the 18 new ones, the model stated a menu path or where the access code is without a source. Most happen right after the app opens the access-code form, in replies like "You'll find the code on the printer's screen in its network or LAN settings."

**Likely cause (my hypothesis, not tested).** The old standing prompt said "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form." I deleted it as a procedure sentence. The Bambu skill's line about the form says to type the code from the printer's screen into it, but it doesn't say "briefly". So the model now explains where to find the code, from memory and with no source.

**`change-then-connect` is the other loss.** All three new misses are the test backend's Sources list landing after the Choices line, which follows a web search. That happens more often now because the skill is in the chat from the first message.

**Proposed fix, not applied:** make the Bambu skill's form line say "Say briefly to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note." Then rerun the six Bambu connect cases on old and new code, 10 runs each, on the subscription.

The logs and these counts are in `connection-skill-at-add-time.md` in the shared notes folder. Nothing is committed.

def reply_problems(reply):
    """How a reply breaks the prompt's rules for every reply: a "Choices:" line
    the page would show as text or draw wrongly (replyChoices.ts), or internal
    words."""
    problems = []
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()

    if found is None and "Choices:" in reply:

    if found is not None:

content.text:
Most of the gap between old and new code came from the test runner, not from my change. With both runner fixes, the old code (e27c962864) passes 382 of 390 runs and the new code 379. Before the fixes it was 371 against 355. Both fixes are in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, uncommitted.

**Choices check.** When the model ends a reply with "Choices:" followed only by a source list, the check now passes it. A source list here means a "Sources:" heading and/or lines of markdown links. Choices followed by any other text still fails. The same rule applies to the two other checks that read the last line: the connect offer after adding, and the Done chip. Two offline tests cover it, one where sources follow Choices and passes, one where other text follows and fails. All 17 offline tests pass.

All 48 Choices misses in today's logs were a source list, and all 48 pass now. On the subscription, `change-then-connect` then passed 10 of 10, and 6 of those replies had a source list.

**Narrower menu-path rule.** In the judge's question, the menu-path sentence now uses Kenneth's agreed wording. It fails only a specific path on the printer or in another program stated as fact with no search or "my guess". General statements are fine, and paths in this app count as sourced. The judge still sees no skill text.

I re-judged only the 23 saved runs the judge had failed for leaving the person stuck (5 old, 18 new), with no new model replies:

| Count of 390 | Old code | New code |
|---|---|---|
| As first judged | 371 | 355 |
| With the narrower rule | 373 | 361 |
| With both fixes | 382 | 379 |

**Cases still different with both fixes (old → new):**

| Case | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `add-many-fit` | 5 | 8 |
| `connect-code-ruled-out` | 9 | 7 |
| `connect-right-code-silent-port` | 8 | 6 |
| `connect-host-no-response` | 10 | 9 |
| `connect-unforeseen-failure` | 10 | 9 |

The new code's remaining misses are of two kinds:
- **A specific path from memory**, which is what the rule is meant to catch. Examples: a Mac's "System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network", "Settings, then the network page" on the printer, and Developer Mode "on the same LAN Only screen".
- **Reasoning slips**: reading "it's the same code" as an answer about the access code when it answered about the address, or stating a cause as fact.

The general "the code is on the printer's screen" replies all pass now. So my earlier guess, that deleting "say briefly to use that form" caused the drop, no longer has much support, and I've dropped that proposed fix.

Two limits on these numbers:
- Runs that passed the first time were not re-judged. The new rule is looser, so they should still pass, but the judge varies from run to run.
- Five runs either way, out of ten per case, is close to how much the counts move between same-day runs.

Results are in `connection-skill-at-add-time.md` in the shared notes folder.

What's the reason why our task resulted in the worse result? I thought our task is supposed to fix the problems when the connection skill was inserted too late, right? Shouldn't I expect the test result to get better?

No, the suite couldn't get better from this change, for two reasons.

**First, the connect cases already had the skill on time.** All 12 `connect-*` cases run in a chat opened with Connect… on a printer. The old code already turned the skill on at the first message in that kind of chat. So for those cases my change didn't move the skill at all. What they did see is the text I changed: sentences taken out of the standing prompt, the Bambu skill's new opening and failure lines, and the merged Moonraker/OctoPrint skill. Text changes like that can move a count either way. They don't make the skill arrive any sooner.

**Second, the suite has no case for the problem we fixed.** The late skill caused trouble in live chats on 2026-11-04. Someone added a printer and connected straight away. The model gave the exact connect offer after they had already asked, and told someone with no key to "use that form", because the standing prompt's steps came before the skill. None of the 39 cases plays that out. The 10 add cases stop at the connect offer or at "Not now", and the old code already passed them 10 of 10. The change chats only connect in `change-then-connect`, which the old code also passed 10 of 10. So the suite could only show whether I broke something, never the improvement.

So from this suite, the right expectation was "no worse", and with the two runner fixes that's roughly what it shows: 382 of 390 old, 379 new. Three runs is within the swing I've seen between same-day runs. The five cases that still differ are Bambu connect chats where a reply named a menu path from memory or misread the person.

To see the improvement, we'd need cases that start connecting during an add chat. One would be a person who adds a Klipper printer, says right away "connect it", and has no key. Another would be someone who asks to connect in the same message they add the printer with. Or the live run in the real app that I proposed earlier. I haven't written those cases. Would you like me to add them and run them on the old and new code on the subscription?
Okay, then commit our change. Save the claude subscription result as the new baseline. Do you know which branch to commit your code to?

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a Bambu Lab printer is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.

Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen. Never ask for it in chat. After the form is sent, the app tries for about 30 seconds, and its note says how it went and whether a code was typed: a form left empty reconnects with the code the app already holds. Answer anything they say meanwhile.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The app's note then says the connection is verified.

## What the tools report

Once they want to connect, read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- Until a printer of this model is heard, `printer_connection_status` listens during the call for up to 30 seconds. `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty after that means nothing was heard in those seconds, which is silence and not a finding: on a real P1S the first announcement once came more than two minutes in. It does not mean the printer is off or absent. The search goes on, and when a printer of this model is heard the app posts a note and starts your next turn. Say you are still looking, ask whether the printer is on, and end your message. Reading the status again listens for another 30 seconds.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_bambu_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- Once `printer_bambu_connect` has opened the form, say to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_bambu_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_bambu_connect` again, which opens the form.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.
